decisions.issues: v04 fits the script beat best: a ground-level shot tight on both bandaged hands clawed into wet grit. The fingers are wrapped and the backs of the hands and wrists are raw red. The left forearm (image right) is heavily crusted with sand and shows no readable mark. The torn ochre tunic hangs open, a rope loop crosses the chest, and the free end trails off into the foam at right. His knees and dhoti sit in the retreating surf. There are no irons, collar, painted text or blood. The face is cropped at the nose, so the eyes stay for 1.3's close-up. What shows matches the sheet: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven stubbled chin, gold ear stud, loose curly hair. Minor flaws: each hand shows only four digits, but one finger reads as buried in the grit, which suits 'dug into' the sand. Only one rope loop is visible where the script asks for two, and he is braced on straight arms rather than slumped. The caption fits the clear sky at top right (about x 0.72-1.0, y 0-0.18). Backup v03 has cleaner five-digit hands and correct identity. Its weaknesses are framing and sequence: it is a wider medium shot, not tight on the hands, and it shows his full face alert and looking off. That pre-empts 1.3's close-up of his cheek pressed to the sand with one eye half open.

Minor issues only. Nagoji's left forefoot is wrapped in a bandage the script never asks for, and in 3.4 his feet are bare, so it is a small continuity slip. The fingers of his right hand splay a little unevenly, and the rope burn on that palm is drawn as a twine-like crosshatch. It still reads as a hand held palm up, bandaged only at the fingers, with a bare palm heel. The Young Fisherman's vest is dark indigo, not the faded blue from 2.4. Everything else holds: Nagoji has a clean-shaven chin, a thick moustache and the gold ear stud, and the rope burns show on his open chest with no rope on him. The Young Fisherman (headband, thin beard) kneels at his right, and the Fisherman (grizzled beard, red lungi, white shoulder cloth) kneels at his left, scraping sand off the inner forearm above the wrist bandage. The brand is not readable. There is no text, noose or gore. The beach, surf, wreck and palms match 2.4. v06 is picked over v05, which is otherwise identical, because its plain indigo and plain red lungis match 2.4 and the likely 3.4 art, while v05 has plaid lungis. There is clear grey sky at top left for the Young Fisherman's balloon, and between Nagoji's head and the Fisherman's for the Fisherman's.

Minor drift only. v07 is the r9 pick (v06) with Nagoji's hand bandages restored. The bandages wrap the fingers and wrists, with a raw heel of the palm, which matches page 3 (3.1, 3.5) and 5.1. v06 is identical but bare-handed, so it breaks that continuity and is only the backup. Carried over from r9: (1) The Fisherman and the Young Fisherman each wear a tiny gold ear drop. Both are clearly not Nagoji (grey beard; headband and chin beard). (2) The Wary Fisherman looks back at the group instead of toward the palms. Everything else is clean. Nagoji is on model: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, gold stud, torn ochre tunic, cream dhoti, no irons, propped on his right forearm. The ridged mark on his left forearm has no legible letters. The bandages sit only on Nagoji; the fishermen's hands are bare. The wreck is the carved-stern hull under a grey storm sky. There is no text and there are no painted boxes. Open sky at top centre (between the wreck and the Young Fisherman) and along the top left takes Nagoji's balloon clear of every face.

Minor drift only. v05 is the r9 pick (v04) with the hand bandages restored, which matches 4.1, 4.4 and page 3. The brand is also softer: in v04 it is crisp looping cord-ridges that read almost as cursive letters, while in v05 it is a blurred ridged patch that suits 'blurred past reading' better. Remaining: (1) Nagoji sits upright with one knee raised and his left forearm on it, not propped on an elbow as in 4.1 and 4.4. This is a small slip in a close shot. (2) The brand shows on the upper/outer side of the LEFT forearm rather than the inner side. The face is on model: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin with a stubble shadow, gold stud, long loose curls. He wears the torn ochre tunic over rope-burn lines and the cream dhoti. His alert, waking upward gaze fits the beat. The bandaged hand has a separate thumb and reads as sound. The grey overcast and surf match the page. There is no text and there are no painted boxes. Large open grey sky in the upper right holds both the caption and the one-word balloon clear of the face.

Minor drift only. v07 is the r9 pick (v06) with Nagoji's finger and wrist bandages added, consistent with 4.1, 4.3 and page 3; the Fisherman's hands stay bare. Carried over: (1) The wreck is a skeletal hulk with standing masts and a tattered sail, not the carved-stern hull in 4.1. It is small at the right edge. (2) The brand is a faint ridged patch on the upper side of the LEFT forearm, not the inner side. It has no legible letters, numerals or cross. (3) The Fisherman's raised brows are subtle, but his wide eyes read as surprise. Nagoji is propped on his right forearm with chin lifted and shoulders squared. He has the thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, the gold stud, the ochre rags and cream dhoti, and no irons. Both bandaged hands have correct finger counts. There is no text and there are no painted boxes. The wide grey sky across the top holds all three balloons above both heads.

Acceptable with minor drift. v07 is the r9 pick (v06) with bandages added to Nagoji's dangling hand, which keeps them continuous from 4.1-4.4 into 5.1. v06 is bare-handed, so the bandages would vanish for one panel. Flaws: (1) The bandage also bled onto the Fisherman's right hand, the one gripping Nagoji's chest. Because the wrap hides the wrist join, a reader will most likely take it for Nagoji's own hand. (2) Nagoji's dangling near arm (his RIGHT) has a pinkish ridged, mottled patch mid-forearm and raw skin above the wrist bandage. It reads as abrasion or rope burn, not gore, but an attentive reader could take it for the brand on the wrong arm. v06 has the same patch. (3) The Young Fisherman's vest and lungi read as one sleeveless indigo tunic. (4) The wreck has standing masts and a tattered sail, unlike 4.1's carved-stern hull. The beat is complete: the grinning Fisherman (white teeth, grey beard, cream vest, shoulder cloth, red lungi) holds Nagoji's shoulders, the Young Fisherman (indigo, headband) holds his legs, and the Wary Fisherman (off-white lungi, brown vest, net) walks ahead. A sand crab sidles in the lower-left foreground. Nagoji is on model: moustache, clean chin, gold stud, no irons. There is no text and there are no painted boxes. Open grey sky at top centre and top right holds both Fisherman balloons clear of every face.

v08 is clean. Nagoji matches his sheet (thick curled moustache, clean chin with light captivity stubble, gold ear stud) and is bare-chested with rope burns, as in 5.5, 6.3 and 6.5. The Woman wrings cloth into the terracotta basin, and the Fisherman (red lungi, shoulder cloth on his left shoulder) relays with a half smile. The upper half is plain wall, so both FISHERMAN balloons fit. Minor: the Woman is medium-built, closer to 5.5 than to the heavy-set woman of 5.4. v09 is rejected: the heavier-Woman edit added a brand-like patch of glyph-like strokes (reads roughly as 'HK') on Nagoji's RIGHT forearm, which is both pseudo-lettering and the wrong arm.

v09 is acceptable. The camera is low beside the mat. The kapitan shows his own left cheek, and the thin scar runs from his left ear to the jaw. He has a white turban and a grey-flecked beard, and wears a pale vest and white mundu with no coat. He looks down at Nagoji's LEFT forearm, which lies inner side up with a blurred, ridged brand (no letters, no cross). Nagoji is bare-chested, looking back, with moustache, clean chin and ear stud. The lungis are plain, matching the neighbouring panels. The upper-left wall is clear for all three captions. Minor: because of foreground perspective, the kapitan does not clearly read as shorter than the Young Fisherman. Nagoji's fingers are bare, while 6.4 wraps them. v08 is the same image, but with checked lungis and parallel diagonal welts where the brand should be.

v07 is acceptable. Nagoji has his eyes closed, the hearth light is on his face, and he matches his sheet (moustache, clean chin, ear stud), bare-chested as elsewhere on the page. Out of focus, the Fisherman and the Young Fisherman turn toward the door. A broad turbaned shadow falls across the floor from a rainy grey doorway, and no figure is visible in it. The upper dark wall is clear for both captions. Minor: Nagoji sits upright cross-legged, while 6.3 and 6.5 show him reclining. A ridged scar patch shows on his left forearm above the bandage, with no letters. v08 is rejected: Nagoji wears the ochre tunic, which the script peels off in 5.5 and which is absent in 6.1, 6.3 and 6.5. Its doorway also shows a sunny beach, contradicting the rain in 6.2 and 6.3.

Minor only. v09 is the grey storm-spent relight of v08, which matches the grey page 4 relights (4.5 v06/v07) and page 6's grey daylight; v08 is identical but sunlit with a turquoise sea. Nagoji is on model: thick moustache, clean chin, gold stud, wrapped hands, no irons. Only one of his legs reads clearly under the dhoti, and the Wary Fisherman's trailing hand touches Nagoji's foot. The Fisherman shows moustache and stubble here, while page 4 gives him a short grey-flecked beard. Captions fit on the grey sea at the top right and the palm fronds at the top left.

Accepted with a caveat. The v06 relight added a small, faint pinkish scuff on Nagoji's LEFT UPPER arm near the elbow, at about x 0.575, y 0.41. It is about 25 px wide. It is not in v05. Zoomed in it looks like a scribble. At print size it reads only as a scrape, but retouch it out if possible, because the brand belongs only on the inner forearm. v05 is clean there but has blue sky and sun, which clashes with grey 5.1 and 5.3. Only two carriers are shown (the Wary Fisherman is absent), which the script allows. Nagoji is on model: moustache, clean chin, stud, wrapped hands. The girl's balloon fits over the thatch and laterite at the upper left, or over the grey sky at top centre.

Minor continuity only. The girl peeking from the doorway wears a beige top and a rust skirt. The whispering girl in 5.2 wears a maroon top and a cream shawl. She is small and reads as shrinking behind the door frame. The Fisherman has a short grey beard here, which matches page 4 but not the stubble in 5.1 and 5.2. v06 is the grey relight and matches 5.1 v09 and 5.2 v06; v05 is the same art in sunlight. Nagoji is on model: moustache, clean chin, stud, wrapped hand, no irons, no visible brand. Both Young Fisherman balloons fit in the grey sky and palm tops above the heads, from top centre to top right.

Both candidates fail. v08 is only a relight of v02. The staging is right: Nagoji carried, left forearm toward camera, rope burns, the Fisherman gesturing, the Woman at the door wringing her cloth, clean sky space at the upper left. The brand is the problem. In both frames it is a distinct reddish-purple monogram of closed loops and script-like strokes on the forearm, and at normal size it reads as painted letters. The v08 fix prompt had explicitly forbidden loops and script-like strokes. Earlier root reviews rejected letter-like and reddish brands. The Woman also has glossy red lipstick-like lips instead of a matte betel stain, and her grey hair looks like a short loose bob with no visible low knot.
decisions.correction: Edit the attached v08 frame and keep every figure, face, pose, costume, prop, the grey overcast light and the composition exactly as they are; change only these details. The brand on the inner side of Nagoji's LEFT forearm, a hand's width above the bandaged wrist, currently looks like a reddish outlined monogram of looped strokes: replace it with a pale, irregular, roughly oval patch of old healed burn scar about the size of a large coin, lighter than the surrounding skin (whitish-tan, slightly shiny, never red, pink, purple or outlined), its surface puckered with short, broken, uneven raised ridges running in different directions, with no closed loops, no smooth curves, no strokes that form letters or symbols, no numerals and not a cross, so it reads only as a blurred, unreadable old burn; add nothing to his upper arm, outer forearm or right arm. Make the Woman's lips matte and uneven, a dull reddish-brown betel stain darker at the corners, not glossy red lipstick, keeping the faint half-smile at one corner, and show her grey-streaked hair drawn back into a loose low knot at the nape. Draw no text, balloons or boxes, and keep the grey sky at the upper left and the thatch along the top clear for lettering.
